best_for: Owners of SteelSeries mice, keyboards and headsets on Windows who want one app for lighting, macros and audio, plus gamers after the free Sonar mixer.
description:
SteelSeries GG is the companion app from SteelSeries, the gaming gear company. It brings the company's gaming services into one window, so you can set up your gear, tune your sound and handle your clips without opening separate programs.

The 3D Aim Trainer holds hundreds of exercises meant to sharpen your aim in first-person shooters. Moments lets you share the clips you save with friends, wherever you like to post them. GG also connects to Discord so your team can hear you clearly, and its game-based profiles and presets are meant to help on any device, not just SteelSeries gear.

points.title: Free, but some parts need the gear
points.text: SteelSeries says GG is free to download and use. Some features only work if you own SteelSeries devices.

points.title: Four tools in one app
points.text: Engine sets up lighting, audio and macros on SteelSeries gear. Sonar tunes game audio, Moments clips and shares gameplay, and the 3D Aim Trainer runs aim drills.

points.title: An account opens the extras
points.text: Basic device settings work without an account. SteelSeries says an account gives you advanced settings and its apps, such as Sonar, Moments, the 3D Aim Trainer and giveaways.

points.title: Sonar is a Windows tool
points.text: Sonar adds a parametric EQ, a mixer with ChatMix and per-app routing, AI noise cancellation and spatial audio. Its page lists Windows 10 (RS5 or newer) and offers only a Windows download.

points.title: Windows specs are modest
points.text: GG needs Windows 10 RS5 or newer, an Intel Core i5-2xxx or AMD FX-4xxx class CPU, 8 GB of RAM, 700 MB of disk space and a broadband connection. The installer is 64-bit and installs for all users.

points.title: The Mac build trails Windows
points.text: The Mac package is universal, for Intel and Apple Silicon, but at review time it was version 108.3.0 against 124.0.0 on Windows. The Windows listing keeps 138 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
